instruction: I have compiled a list of invitees for our upcoming baby shower. You can find it in "~/documents/personal" in my file system. The email template for the invitations is saved in my Gmail drafts. Replace the placeholders in it marked by curly braces with the relevant details and send invitation emails, individually to each person.
notes: Reference solution has 11 APIs, so the invitee list is assumed to contain 3 people (8 fixed steps + one gmail.send_email per invitee). The invitees are declared as domain constants so that supervisor-complete-task can enumerate every goal condition without quantifiers; for a different invitee count add/remove constants, email/body objects, init links and goal atoms. Static init facts (in-directory, invitee-in-file, invitee-email, draft-subject, body-for) only link runtime-bound objects structurally; their actual values become usable only after the gating lookups (show_directory -> known-id of file, show_file -> file-read, show_drafts -> known-id of draft, show_draft -> template-read). gmail.send_email is called once per invitee with email_addresses = [invitee email] (exactly one recipient), subject taken verbatim from the draft, and body = draft body with the curly-brace placeholders filled from the invitee's details. The draft must not be edited and no new drafts are created (deleting the template draft is tolerated but not modeled). complete_task is called without an answer.
